name: Change Audit — Removable Media Plugged or Denied (Kaspersky Device Control)
Endpoint — Security Agent (AV/EDR) Files Deleted or Replaced
description:
Attacker objective
Evade detection by deleting, replacing or tampering with the endpoint antivirus / EDR agent's files so protection and telemetry stop.

Attack logic
Antivirus and EDR agents install their binaries and configuration under known program directories. Deleting or replacing those files is a direct attempt to disable endpoint protection — a common early defense-evasion step.

Why this detection works
File-integrity monitoring records deletion and creation of files in the security-agent directories, surfacing agent tampering at the filesystem level even without process context.

False positives
Legitimate agent auto-update, upgrade or reinstall (which deletes and recreates agent files).

Tuning
Allowlist verified agent-update/maintenance windows and deployment tooling; prioritise deletions on hosts with no concurrent update; correlate with the agent's own health/heartbeat and with a loss of endpoint telemetry.

Required telemetry
File Integrity Monitoring (fim.event): file.path (security-agent program directories), event.action, host.name.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. host.name is the affected endpoint; review which agent files were deleted/created and whether an update was scheduled.
2. Correlate with the agent's own status (e.g. Kaspersky 'endpoint unmanaged') and with any loss of EDR/AV telemetry from the host.
3. Unexplained deletion of agent files is defense evasion — isolate and investigate the host.
false_positives: Legitimate agent auto-update, upgrade or reinstall (which deletes and recreates agent files).
query: event.dataset:"fim.event" and event.action:("deleted" or "created") and (file.path:*Kaspersky* or file.path:*Elastic* or file.path:*Defender* or file.path:*Endgame*)

name: Kaspersky — Behavioral Threat Blocked (Adaptive Anomaly Control)
description:
Attacker objective
Execute code through a living-off-the-land chain — for example a scripting interpreter launched from an unusual parent (WMI, Office) with an encoded command — that deviates from the endpoint's normal behaviour.

Attack logic
Kaspersky Adaptive Anomaly Control learns each host's normal behaviour and blocks anomalous process actions such as an interpreter being spawned from an atypical parent process. A block indicates behaviour abnormal for that endpoint.

Why this detection works
The behavioural rule name, together with the source and target process paths and the target command line, identifies the exact LOLBin/interpreter chain that was blocked.

False positives
Legitimate management or monitoring tooling that uses the same chain (e.g. WMI-based administration) on a host where it is not part of the learned baseline.

Tuning
Exclude verified management/monitoring hosts and service accounts; review the target command line (often encoded) before dismissing.

Required telemetry
Kaspersky Security Center CEF (GNRL_EV_ADSEC_DETECT): RuleName, SrcProcPath, TrgProcPath, target command line, destination.domain, destination.user.name.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. Examine the source process → target process and the target command line; decode any encoded command.
2. An encoded interpreter launch from WMI, Office or another unusual parent is likely malicious — investigate the host.
3. Confirm whether the host runs sanctioned management tooling that would explain the chain.
false_positives: Legitimate management or monitoring tooling that uses the same chain (e.g. WMI-based administration) on a host where it is not part of the learned baseline.

name: Kaspersky — Endpoint Dropped Off Central Management (Agent Unmanaged)
description:
Attacker objective
Evade endpoint protection by removing or disabling the security agent so the host stops reporting to central management and loses protection and telemetry.

Attack logic
When an endpoint stops being managed by the central security server, its protection state and event stream are lost. This can be benign (a long-offline or decommissioned device) or an attacker disabling the agent to operate unobserved.

Why this detection works
The management server emits an event, naming the device, whenever a host becomes unmanaged — a tripwire for lost endpoint visibility.

False positives
A device legitimately offline for a long period, reimaged, or decommissioned.

Tuning
Correlate with asset lifecycle/change records; prioritise servers and recently-active hosts that suddenly become unmanaged.

Required telemetry
Kaspersky Security Center CEF (KLSRV_HOST_OUT_CONTROL; the affected device is named in the event message).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. Identify the named device from the event message.
2. Confirm whether it was decommissioned or simply offline; if unexplained, treat as possible agent tampering and investigate the host directly.
3. A server or active workstation going unmanaged is higher priority.
false_positives: A device legitimately offline for a long period, reimaged, or decommissioned.

name: Kaspersky — Malware Detected on Endpoint
description: Detects Kaspersky Endpoint Security identifying malware on a managed endpoint (virus/trojan/etc.). The alert carries the malware name, file path, SHA256 hash, endpoint and user — including high-value endpoints such as ATMs and banking servers.
note:
## Investigation
1. `deviceCustomString1` is the malware/VirusName, `filePath` the object, `deviceCustomString4` the SHA256, `destination.domain` the endpoint and `destination.user.name` the user.
2. Pivot the SHA256 to threat intel; check the endpoint's process/PowerShell (4688/4104) and network activity for the same window.
## Response
Isolate the endpoint if the threat is a stealer/RAT/ransomware, verify remediation, and hunt for lateral movement.
author: raadabujaish

name: Kaspersky Malware Not Cured
description: This rule detects when Kaspersky finds a malicious object and does not cure it.

name: Kaspersky — Malware or Malicious Object Detected on an Endpoint
description:
Attacker objective
Deliver and run malware on an endpoint, or drive a user to a malicious site, as part of initial access, execution or command-and-control.

Attack logic
Kaspersky Endpoint Security detects known malware, heuristically-identified trojans, and access to malicious or blacklisted URLs. A detection means a real threat reached the endpoint, whether or not it was blocked.

Why this detection works
The endpoint antivirus verdict carries the threat name and the affected host and user — a high-fidelity indicator that a threat was present on the endpoint.

False positives
Low-risk adware/riskware ('not-a-virus') detections, or a benign file matching a heuristic signature.

Tuning
Optionally exclude 'not-a-virus'/adware verdicts to focus on high-severity malware; prioritise detections that were not disinfected/cured.

Required telemetry
Kaspersky Security Center CEF: cef.device.event_class_id (GNRL_EV_VIRUS_*), VirusName, destination.domain (endpoint), destination.user.name.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. destination.domain = the affected endpoint; destination.user.name = the user; the threat name is in the event.
2. Confirm the object was blocked/cured; if not cured, isolate the host and run a full scan.
3. For a malicious-URL verdict, review the browser/process that made the request and hunt for follow-on C2.
false_positives: Low-risk adware/riskware ('not-a-virus') detections, or a benign file matching a heuristic signature.
query: observer.vendor:"KasperskyLab" and cef.device.event_class_id:("GNRL_EV_VIRUS_FOUND" or "GNRL_EV_VIRUS_FOUND_AND_BLOCKED" or "GNRL_EV_OBJECT_BLOCKED" or "GNRL_EV_OBJECT_NOTCURED" or "GNRL_EV_OBJECT_DELETED" or "GNRL_EV_OBJECT_QUARANTINED")

name: Kaspersky — Malware Remediation Failed / Active Infection
description: Fires on Kaspersky's GNRL_EV_OBJECT_NOTCURED event — a detected malicious object that Kaspersky could not disinfect, delete, or quarantine, meaning the malware remains live on the endpoint. Unlike a normal detected-and-cleaned event, a failed remediation is an active-infection state that needs hands-on response. The rule matches the Kaspersky vendor event code in CEF. ATT&CK mapping is approximate — the signal is an unremediated infection, not a specific delivery technique.
note:
### Investigation
1. Identify the infected host (destination.domain) and user (destination.user.name), and the malware file (filePath) and threat name.
2. Confirm remediation truly failed (deviceCustomString4/result) versus a transient quarantine issue.
3. Determine whether the object is executing (disk in a user/temp path) or dormant (inside a locked archive/backup on read-only media).
4. Isolate the host if the object is live; correlate other Kaspersky events (uninstall, repeated detections) and network indicators from the same host.
5. Escalate to IR for a confirmed active infection on a production/banking endpoint.

### False positives / benign
Kaspersky can report NOTCURED for an item inside a locked archive, backup, or read-only media it cannot clean but which is not executing — a quarantine-permission edge case rather than a live infection. Distinguish by the filePath (temp/user/startup path and an executable versus an archive on read-only media) and whether the object recurs or spreads. Investigate each rather than suppressing the event code, since a genuine unremediated infection uses the same signal.

### Notes
Highlighted-field enrichment pending: Kaspersky CEF host/file carriers are sparse estate-wide (deviceCustomString1 0%, filePath 1%); verify the populated carriers on the NOTCURED event slice before adding them.
author: raadabujaish

name: Kaspersky — Multiple Threat Detections on One Endpoint
description:
Attacker objective
Operate on a compromised endpoint that is generating several endpoint-security detections in a short window — repeated malware, blocked behaviours or network attacks.

Attack logic
An isolated antivirus or behavioural detection may be a single blocked threat. One host producing multiple detections in a short window indicates active, repeated malicious activity rather than a one-off block.

Why this detection works
Aggregating threat detections per host over the endpoint-security stream elevates a cluster of detections on the same endpoint into a high-confidence compromise signal.

False positives
A host repeatedly visiting the same malicious-advertising domain, or a noisy adware infection generating many low-severity detections.

Tuning
Exclude low-risk adware verdicts; raise the per-host detection threshold if noisy.

Required telemetry
Kaspersky Security Center CEF (virus, behavioural and network-attack event classes; destination.domain).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. Review the host's detections (threat names, processes, attack names) listed in the alert.
2. Multiple distinct detection types on one host is a strong compromise indicator — isolate and perform full incident response.
3. Correlate the host with its Windows/AD activity for scope.
false_positives: A host repeatedly visiting the same malicious-advertising domain, or a noisy adware infection generating many low-severity detections.
query:
FROM logs-cef.log-* METADATA _id, _index, _version
| WHERE observer.vendor == "KasperskyLab" AND destination.domain IS NOT NULL AND cef.device.event_class_id IN ("GNRL_EV_VIRUS_FOUND","GNRL_EV_VIRUS_FOUND_AND_BLOCKED","GNRL_EV_OBJECT_BLOCKED","GNRL_EV_VIRUS_OBJECT_NOTCURED","GNRL_EV_ADSEC_DETECT","GNRL_EV_ATTACK_DETECTED")
| STATS detections = COUNT(), distinct_types = COUNT_DISTINCT(cef.device.event_class_id), types = VALUES(cef.device.event_class_id), threat_names = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString1), users = VALUES(destination.user.name) BY destination.domain
| WHERE detections >= 3

name: Kaspersky — Network Attack Detected Against an Endpoint
description:
Attacker objective
Exploit a network-facing service on an endpoint or server (remote code execution, scanning, brute-force) for initial access or lateral movement.

Attack logic
Kaspersky Network Threat Protection (host network IPS) detects and blocks known network exploits and attacks directed at the protected host.

Why this detection works
The attack signature name, the victim host and the attacker IP together are a high-fidelity indicator that an exploitation attempt reached the host.

False positives
An authorised vulnerability scanner triggering network-attack signatures.

Tuning
Allowlist sanctioned scanner sources; prioritise attacks targeting servers over workstations.

Required telemetry
Kaspersky Security Center CEF (GNRL_EV_ATTACK_DETECTED): AttackName, destination.domain (victim), AttackerIPv4, AttackedPort/Protocol.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. The attack name, victim host (destination.domain) and attacker IP are in the event.
2. Confirm whether the targeted service is exposed; even if blocked, profile the attacker and hunt for follow-on activity on the victim.
3. Prioritise attacks against internet-facing or high-value servers.
false_positives: An authorised vulnerability scanner triggering network-attack signatures.

name: Kaspersky — Endpoint Protection Agent Uninstalled
description: Fires when Kaspersky reports KLNAG_EV_INV_APP_UNINSTALLED for one of its own protection components (Kaspersky Endpoint Security or Network Agent) — the security agent being removed from an endpoint. Removing EDR blinds monitoring and typically precedes further malicious activity on the host. The rule matches the Kaspersky uninstall event where the application name is a protection component. Maps to ATT&CK Defense Evasion T1562.001 (Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools).
note:
### Investigation
1. Identify the endpoint (destination.domain) and which component (message) was removed.
2. Check for an approved decommission/reimage/migration change window covering the uninstall.
3. Determine whether protection was reinstalled shortly after (legitimate migration) or the host went dark (evasion).
4. Correlate host activity immediately after removal — new processes, logons, or the NOTCURED/infection signal — for what the blind window enabled.
5. Escalate if there is no change record, especially on a server or privileged workstation.

### False positives / benign
Sanctioned decommission, reimage, version migration, or IT uninstalling to reinstall all generate this event legitimately. Distinguish by a matching change record and whether the agent is reinstalled promptly on the same host, versus a standalone removal with no follow-up reinstall and subsequent unmonitored activity. Do not allowlist hosts — an attacker removes the agent on exactly the hosts IT also services; correlate to the change window instead.

### Notes
Highlighted-field enrichment pending: verify populated Kaspersky CEF carriers on the uninstall event slice; the initiating account is absent from this event (pivot to host 4688).
author: raadabujaish
query: observer.vendor:"KasperskyLab" and event.code:"KLNAG_EV_INV_APP_UNINSTALLED" and cef.extensions.message:("Kaspersky" or "KES" or "Endpoint Security" or "Network Agent")

name: Kaspersky — Repeated Blocked Application Launches on One Endpoint
description: ≥10 application-control launch denials on one endpoint in 24h — a user or malware repeatedly trying to run blocked software. Baseline: HQ-MOHAMMADADEL 28/7d, Player-403-1 24/7d would alert; the estate tail (2-4/7d) stays quiet. Suppression 24h so a persistent offender pages once daily.
author: JCB Detection Engineering

name: Kaspersky — Virus Outbreak Detected
description: Detects Kaspersky Security Center raising a Virus Outbreak — its own correlation that the same or many threats are detected across multiple endpoints in a short period, indicating malware spreading through the environment (worm/ransomware propagation).
note:
## Investigation
1. Review the outbreak scope (affected hosts/threat) in Kaspersky Security Center.
2. Identify patient-zero and the propagation vector.
## Response
Contain affected network segments, accelerate signature/patch deployment, and initiate mass IR.
author: raadabujaish

name: Malware Infection
description: Detects when the same malware threat is detected on 5 or more unique hosts , indicating potential widespread malware infection or outbreak across the network. This helps identify rapidly spreading malware campaigns or coordinated attacks impacting multiple endpoints.
